content: Salsalate is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, particularly in individuals who take it for extended periods. These cardiovascular events can occur without warning and may be fatal. Inform your doctor if you or your family have a history of heart disease, heart failure, heart attack, or stroke, or if you have high cholesterol, high blood pressure, diabetes, or if you smoke. Seek emergency medical attention immediately if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech. Do not take salsalate immediately before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. NSAIDs like salsalate can cause ulcers, bleeding, or perforations in the stomach or intestines, which may occur without warning and can be fatal. The risk is higher in older adults, those in poor health, smokers, or individuals who consume large amounts of alcohol. Notify your doctor if you are taking anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), or oral steroids (e.g., prednisone, dexamethasone). Also, inform your doctor if you have a history of ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or other bleeding disorders. Stop taking salsalate and contact your doctor if you experience stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting blood or material resembling coffee grounds, blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools. Your doctor will monitor your symptoms and may order tests to assess your response to salsalate. Always follow your doctor’s instructions and take the medication exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed. It may take three to four days to feel the full effects of the medication. If your symptoms do not improve or worsen, contact your doctor. Salsalate is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and other inflammatory conditions. It works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. Take salsalate orally, usually two to three times a day, with food or milk to prevent stomach upset. Take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, but skip it if it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Before taking salsalate, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, aspirin, other NSAIDs, or any of its ingredients. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, especially those mentioned in the warning section. Notify your doctor if you have asthma, gout, kidney or liver disease, or swelling in your extremities. Salsalate should not be given to children or teenagers with chickenpox, flu, or recent varicella vaccination due to the risk of Reye’s syndrome. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking salsalate, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking salsalate. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while on this medication. Mild side effects of salsalate include diarrhea and dizziness. Notify your doctor if these symptoms persist or worsen. Serious side effects include ringing in the ears, hearing loss, difficulty breathing or swallowing, shortness of breath, hoarseness, rapid heartbeat, unexplained weight gain, swelling of the face or extremities, rash, hives, blisters, itching, unusual bleeding or bruising, pale or cold skin, fever, nausea, headache, extreme fatigue, weakness, loss of appetite, upper right abdominal pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, discolored or bloody urine, back pain, or painful urination. If you experience any of these, stop taking salsalate and contact your doctor immediately. Store salsalate in its original container, tightly closed, at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual collapses or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose include ringing in the ears, dizziness, headache, confusion, extreme fatigue, sweating, rapid breathing, extreme thirst, muscle cramps, fainting, flushing, or loss of consciousness. Before undergoing any laboratory tests, inform your doctor and lab personnel that you are taking salsalate. Do not share this medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
